title: Three-way alignment playbook (scratch)
content:
Context and goals:
- Quick scratch for an asymmetric prep: product + serving runtime (eng) + applied-ml sync.
- Goal: get to a shared decision on 3 risky surface areas for H2 roadmap before exec sync: (1) quantized model baseline for chat endpoints, (2) prioritized rollout order for model variants (latency vs quality), (3) telemetry/eval gating for canary.

Participants to invite (short list):
- Rina (product host) — bring customer signal + OKR alignment
- Samir (serving runtime lead) — capacity & SLO constraints
- Mateo (applied ML) — model perf / eval thresholds
- Ops: optional (if rollback plan changes)
- Me (Aria) — facilitator + note taker

Agenda (30–40 min):
1) 5 min — Shared framing: what decision do we need by Friday
2) 10 min — Quick data: latency/cost delta for quantized v.s. fp16 on p4/p8 (Samir)
3) 8 min — Quality deltas across prompt families; show eval breakouts (Mateo)
4) 7 min — Product constraints: customer tiers, SLA tolerances, migration windows (Rina)
5) 5–10 min — Decision and next steps: rollout order + gating metrics

Prep notes (things I need before the call):
- Samir: run a 2-hour micro-benchmark with the new kernel on 8k seqs for the 2 candidate models; report p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate. Slack thread tag: #infra-quant-bench.
- Mateo: share the small eval slice (legal/cs support / conversational search) with per-prompt metric diffs (EM, F1, hallucination score); include examples where quantization broke structured outputs. Put in a gist or confluence table.
- Rina: refresh customer target list (top 5 customers likely to hit latency-sensitive paths) and map to SLA tiers. Short list of customers we can pilot with.
- Me: prepare two decision templates: A) conservative rollout (dedicated first, then hosted), B) aggressive (hosted + fallback).

Hypotheses to test on call:
- H1: Quantized int8 variant reduces cost by ~2.4x while only slightly increasing hallucination risk on long-form prompts.
- H2: Canary gating on per-prompt regression (delta > X%) plus a health signal (p95 latency increase > Y ms) will catch-most regressions without slowing rollout.
- H3: Serving-side caching on prefixes will hide some quantization latency regressions for conversational flows with long histories.

Tradeoffs & risks to surface quickly:
- Quality vs cost: if quantization regresses structured outputs (JSON/table), product must restrict feature for higher tiers.
- Rollout complexity: more model variants == more routing logic and higher operational burden for SRE.
- Telemetry gaps: we only have lab evals for some prompt families; production signal for hallucination is weak. Need manual review sample plan.

Decision criteria (proposal):
- Accept quantized baseline if: median downstream metric drop < 2% for core prompts AND no catastrophic structured-output failures in sample of 200.
- Rollout order: Dedicated customers (reserved) -> Beta hosted (selected customers) -> Full hosted.
- Gating: automatic rollback if per-customer error rate increase > 1.5x baseline OR p95 latency > SLO + 50ms for 10m window.

Open questions (to resolve in sync or async):
- What is the exact hallucination proxy we can compute in prod? (Mateo + Observability)
- If we restrict structured-output endpoints to fp16 for all hosted customers, what is cost delta and revenue impact? (Product + Finance)
- Do we need an explicit feature flag per-customer or per-route? Quick debate: per-route is simpler operationally but per-customer is safer.

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Samir: deliver benchmark table + cost calc (ETA: 2026-09-22)
- Mateo: upload eval slices + 20 red/green example pairs (ETA: 2026-09-22)
- Rina: draft pilot customer list + comm plan (ETA: 2026-09-23)
- Aria: synth decision templates + submit to product-review (ETA: 2026-09-23)
- All: sync on Slack thread after call with final notes and PRD link (ETA: 24h after meeting)

Notes-to-self / running log (scratch):
- Keep the meeting <40m — focus on binary decision points.
- Bring up fallback automation: if capacity spike, auto-route to cheaper quantized variant only for low-tier customers. Need Samir to confirm router can do per-tier rules.
- If telemetry proxy is not ready, propose a manual 48h review window during beta.
- Pull sample transcripts for the "hallucination" examples — ask CS to tag 10 transcripts from last month.

Post-meeting follow-up template (to copy/paste into Slack/email):
- TL;DR decision + bullets on action items + who owns what + link to artifacts. Keep <6 bullets.

Quick crumbs to attach in meeting:
- Confluence: PROJECT-ROADMAP-2026 -> section: model-variant-rollout (bookmark)
- GH: repo/issue/482 (tracking rollout automation)
- Slack: #applied-ml / #infra-quant-bench threads (links above)

End of scratchpad. Keep iterative notes here during the call.

-- aria
